hints: Focus on what but-2-ene is, a symmetrical alkene, and remember alkenes can add across the double bond or have it cleaved completely.
Check compound 2 first, as acid-catalysed hydration of CH3CH=CHCH3 with steam gives butan-2-ol in one step.
Now compare mild oxidation for the diol with vigorous hot oxidation for cleavage, and see if both 1 and 3 can also form directly in one step.
walkthrough:
**Draw out the starting alkene**

Think of but-2-ene simply as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3$. The $\text{C}=\text{C}$ double bond is electron rich, so it can undergo addition or oxidation.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3$$

**Test compound 1, the diol**

Cold, dilute, alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ adds two $\text{-OH}$ groups across the double bond in one step. This is dihydroxylation.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3 + [\text{O}] + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_3$$
So 1 is possible.

**Test compound 2, the mono-alcohol**

Steam with concentrated $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ catalyst (or conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ followed by water) adds $\text{H}$ and $\text{OH}$ across the double bond. Because but-2-ene is symmetrical, only butan-2-ol forms.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
So 2 is possible.

**Test compound 3, ethanoic acid**

Hot, concentrated $\text{KMnO}_4$ with acid cleaves the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bond completely. Each $\text{CH}$ end of but-2-ene is oxidised up to a carboxylic acid.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3 + [\text{O}] \rightarrow 2\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$$
So 3 is also possible in a single vigorous oxidation.

**Put it together**

Since 1, 2 and 3 can all be made directly from but-2-ene in just one reaction step (just with different reagents), the combination is 1, 2 and 3.

options.A: Correct. All three are one-step products: 1 by cold dilute KMnO4 dihydroxylation, 2 by acid-catalysed hydration, and 3 by hot concentrated KMnO4 oxidative cleavage to give two molecules of ethanoic acid.
options.B: Incorrect. This option includes only 1 and 2. Students choose this if they forget that vigorous oxidation cleaves an internal alkene like but-2-ene to carboxylic acids, so they wrongly reject 3.
options.C: Incorrect. This option includes only 2 and 3. Students choose this if they confuse mild and vigorous KMnO4 conditions and think the diol 1 needs more than one step.
options.D: Incorrect. This option includes only 1. Students choose this if they only remember the test for unsaturation with KMnO4 and miss both the hydration route to 2 and the cleavage route to 3.
